newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise, but gains seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise, but gains seen limited.

text.p: Danish bond prices climbed in early trade on Tuesday, but dealers saw activity likely to limited during the day with players keeping an eye on the Fed's FOMC meeting although few seriously expected a rate change.

They said that domestic politics were also contributing to the cautious mood, with investors suspecting that next week's 1998 budget proposal would be too generous and also made uneasy by news that a referendum on EU treaty amendments would only be held next May.
"That prolongs uncertainty about Denmark's status," a dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.18 point from Monday's close at 112.68, yielding 6.05 percent, at 0830 GMT. The seven percent 2007 paper, which becomes the benchmark on September 1, was 0.18 point higher too at 105.58, yielding 6.24 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 62 basis points. The crown traded at 3.8081 per mark, firming a whisker from Monday's closing 3.8085.
